posts.headline: Week 11 Preview: Vitside Mafia vs Gridiron Geeks Is the Game
posts.body: The bye race runs through Vitside Mafia and Gridiron Geeks, and I'm telling you who wins it. Plus picks for all eight matchups and the NFL games that decide them.
content: Boom! Week 11 is here, and I'm told the biggest fight on the board is for a first-round bye, not a playoff spot.
Vitside Mafia and Gridiron Geeks are chasing the same prize, and this is the game that tells us who gets it. Check the live scoreboard all Sunday to see it unfold.

story: League sources tell me this is the one. Vitside Mafia (11-2) and Gridiron Geeks (10-3) are both chasing a first-round bye, and the bye odds swing hard in this game.
Vitside Mafia's bye odds are about 45 percent right now, and a win pushes that to about 79 percent. Gridiron Geeks sit around 37 percent and could jump to about 65 with a win.
The NFL game that decides it is MIA at BUF, where Josh Allen (28.8 projected) and Tyler Bass (6.6) carry Vitside Mafia's hopes. Allen is the engine of that roster and it shows.
Gridiron Geeks counter with Jordan Love (22.1) and Daniel Jones (21.2), plus Ja'Marr Chase (16.9) catching passes in Cincinnati. That is a lot of firepower.
Gridiron Geeks lead the all-time series 8-7, but Vitside Mafia took the only playoff meeting. Money is nice, but this bye is better.
My pick: Vitside Mafia, 168-149. The projections say 161 to 127, and Allen gets the edge.
Pacific Pigskins (9-4) are sitting on a three-game losing streak, and they should bounce back against Dead Cap Walking (2-11).
NO at CHI is the NFL game to watch, with Caleb Williams and Colston Loveland both on the field.
My pick: Pacific Pigskins, 131-94.
Running down the Dream (9-4) are chasing a bye at about 9 percent, and they have Brock Purdy and Christian McCaffrey in MIN at SF to help.
The Mariachi Ninjas have won three straight meetings, so this one is not a gimme.
My pick: Running down the Dream, 133-96.
Da Dangsters (9-4) host Midwestside Connection (6-7) in a game that barely moves the playoff needle for the favorite but matters a lot to the underdog.
My pick: Da Dangsters, 128-117.
Computer Jocks (6-7) have won the last six meetings, and Music City Mafia (2-11) has lost four straight. Bet on the streak.
My pick: Computer Jocks, 127-101.
Cowboy Up (8-5) are on a four-game win streak and sit at about 95 percent playoff odds. Dark Magicians of Chaos (5-8) have won the last four meetings, though, and Dak Prescott is a problem.
My pick: Cowboy Up, 109-104. Joe Burrow's 30.6 projected is the difference.
Wascawy Wabbits (10-3) have won three straight, and Maverick (2-11) can't stop them. Trevor Lawrence and Deshaun Watson do the heavy lifting.
My pick: Wascawy Wabbits, 150-112.
Bring The Pain (3-10) have Jahmyr Gibbs (20.6) and Emeka Egbuka (10.6) on the field in TB at DET. That is a real chance to climb out of the cellar.
My pick: Bring The Pain, 118-116.

posts.headline: Week 10 Waiver Wire: Silence Across The League
posts.body: Not a single claim, not a single dollar spent. Schefter breaks down why Week 10's waiver wire went dead and where owners should be looking instead.
content: Boom, the waiver wire was quiet in Week 10, and I mean completely quiet. Zero claims, zero free agent pickups, zero dollars spent across The League.
I'm told owners are sitting on their current benches and hoping the next wave of drops gives them a reason to move. Money is nice, but championships are better, and nobody added a thing this week.

Every add in this league costs at least the $425K league-minimum salary, so there's no such thing as a free pickup. That makes a week like this look even more deliberate, because nobody wanted to pay the price.
